solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Transport lots of collected works

definitions.meaning: first meaning: buses, a form of public transport
second meaning: omnibus editions, single volumes gathering several works

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase about carrying books around, but it splits after 'Transport' into two separate meanings of the same plural word.
explanation.definitionFit: Omnibus is an old word for a bus and also a publishing term for a volume collecting several works by one author.

clue.text: Surpass alfresco party

parts.note: alfresco means out of doors, outside, so out
a do is a party, as in 'a big do'

explanation.surface: Beating everyone by throwing an outdoor party.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone is to do better than them, to beat or exceed them.

clue.text: Few sense concern about press meetings

indicators.note: about here means all around, so the letters of the three words are scattered into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A worry that few people show judgement over gatherings of journalists.
explanation.definitionFit: Briefings held for journalists, where officials answer reporters' questions, are the meetings of the press.

clue.text: Two sentences for the avian community

indicators.note: Two says the word sentences supplies a pair of pieces, here two different prison terms set side by side

parts.note: bird (rhyming slang bird-lime, time) and life are both British slang for a prison sentence; this piece is the first
life is a life sentence, the longest prison term

explanation.surface: Two lines of writing about birds, as if summarising a nature book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentences' are not grammatical ones but prison terms, two different slang words for a spell inside, placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds collectively, the feathered population of an area, are what avian (bird-related) community describes.

clue.text: Very loud, but ultimately quiet

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so tired'
F is forte, the musical direction for loud

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it, but

explanation.surface: A contradictory description of a sound that is very loud yet in the end quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft sound is a quiet, gentle one, the opposite of loud.

clue.text: Camp clearing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a place where people have settled, a colony or encampment
second meaning: the paying off of a debt or resolving of a dispute

explanation.walkthrough: 'Clearing' suggests an open space in a forest beside a camp, but it means paying off what is owed.
explanation.definitionFit: A settlement is both a small community of settlers and the payment that resolves an account or legal claim.

clue.text: Herb associated with Don in Essex town

indicators.note: the herb's name goes together with Don to make the town, so Don is the part taken away to leave it

parts.note: Basildon is a town in Essex, a county east of London
taken as written: the letters of Don

explanation.surface: A herb linked with a man called Don who lives in an Essex town.
explanation.walkthrough: Basildon is a town in Essex, in eastern England; the herb plus DON spells it, so take DON away.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is a fragrant culinary herb, much used in Italian cooking and pesto.

clue.text: Papal letters bishop cut up

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: to cut is to sever

explanation.surface: Letters from the Pope that a bishop tore to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut up' looks like one phrase meaning shredded, but 'cut' is the verb to sever and 'up', in a down clue, reads it from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A breve is a letter from the Pope, less formal than a bull, sealed with the papal seal.

clue.text: Ram, potentially, indicator of 50s Ford car

parts.note: a sign is an indicator, something that points to something
the Ford Zodiac was a British Ford saloon launched in the 1950s; with 'the' it is a car name

explanation.surface: A ram mascot as the badge on a classic 1950s Ford.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ford Zodiac was a British car of the 1950s, so the car is 'the Zodiac' and its 'indicator' is a sign.
explanation.definitionFit: The ram stands for Aries, one of the twelve astrological constellations of the zodiac, so it is an example.

clue.text: Most of Rheingold arranged with new, alternative opera name

indicators.note: arranged means the remaining letters are put in a different order
most of signals that the last letter of Rheingold is dropped

explanation.surface: Reworking the Wagner opera Rheingold into a different opera title.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the final D of RHEINGOLD ('Most of'), add N for 'new', then 'arranged' scrambles RHEINGOLN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lohengrin is another Wagner opera, separate from the Ring cycle that includes Das Rheingold.

clue.text: Reliable fellow's powerful tugboat?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person others can lean on in difficult times
second, punning meaning: a tower (something that tows) of great strength

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: read 'tower' as a thing that tows, rhyming with 'grower', not a tall building.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower of strength is an idiom for a dependable person who gives support in a crisis.

clue.text: Ready to work briefly at one time with everyone

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the word goes

parts.note: once means at one time, formerly
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Someone always available for duty, glancing back to when the whole team was free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' is the crossword signal to lop the final letter off the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on call means being available to be summoned for duty, as doctors and engineers are outside normal hours.

clue.text: Rodgers and Hart song: low, low number

parts.note: low means feeling down, blue
to low is to make the noise a cow makes, moo
N is the mathematical symbol for a number

explanation.surface: A description of a famous song as gloomy and melancholy.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'low' looks like emphasis, but the first is the mood and the second is a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue Moon is a 1934 popular standard written by songwriters Richard Rodgers and Lorenz Hart.

clue.text: Reporting from 2 maybe sinking beers during short trip

indicators.note: during places the beers within the shortened trip
short means the last letter of the word is clipped

parts.note: a journey is a trip
ales are beers

explanation.surface: Journalists from a press briefing downing beer on a quick outing.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' refers to the answer of 2 Down, NEWS CONFERENCES, whose reporters write this style. 'Sinking', as in drinking, just colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalese is the clichéd writing style of newspapers, the kind of prose filed after press briefings.

clue.text: Potential difficulties from Moscow and far north somehow

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some unspecified way, a reordering

parts.note: taken as written
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Likely troubles arising from Russia's capital and its remote northern regions.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening a can of worms is an idiom for starting something that will create many complicated problems.

clue.text: Reportedly cold, long for one to supply wood

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as heard, a sound-alike spelt differently

parts.note: chilly means cold
to pine is to long for something

explanation.surface: Someone, apparently cold, yearns for a log supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: CHILLY spoken sounds like the country name CHILE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chile pine, or monkey puzzle tree, is a conifer, and any tree is a source of timber.

clue.text: Extremely short, angular celebrity

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters, of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: Describing a famous person as very short and bony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for 'short', but it takes the ends of 'short' and 'angular'.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a famous performer, the leading name of film or stage.

clue.text: Brown's old joke

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a reddish-brown colour, as of the nut
second meaning: a stale, overused joke or story

explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown's' reads as a person's name, perhaps a comic with stale material, but it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Chestnut names a reddish-brown shade and, by idiom, a hackneyed anecdote told too often.

clue.text: High liver from Central Tibet? Wrong

indicators.note: central signals the middle letters of Tibet, its ends dropped

parts.note: X is the cross marked against a wrong answer

explanation.surface: A query about whether a creature from the middle of Tibet is wrongly identified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High liver' reads like someone who lives luxuriously, but it means an animal living at altitude.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibex is a wild mountain goat found at high altitudes in the Alps and Himalayas.

clue.text: Plant one of many used in café

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a climbing vegetable plant grown for its pods

definitions.text: one of many used in café
definitions.meaning: second, cryptic meaning: café is a French word, and coffee is made from many beans

explanation.walkthrough: Café is French both for coffee and a coffee shop; the beans ground to make it are, playfully, French.
explanation.definitionFit: The French bean is a cultivated plant, also called green or string bean, whose pods are eaten.

clue.text: Hoover, say, setting me back about £25

indicators.note: about means around, so the reversed word wraps the slang sum
setting with back, as in setting a clock back, means the word me is turned round
back with setting means the word me is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written: the letters of me
a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds

explanation.surface: A vacuum cleaner purchase costing about twenty-five pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: A pony is British slang for £25. Hoover, a brand that became the word for a vacuum cleaner, is the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoover is named after its maker, so the brand is a word derived from a person's name.

clue.text: King and knight in order losing heads for model

indicators.note: losing heads means each of the two words drops its first letter

parts.note: Rex is Latin for king, as in the royal cipher
a Templar is a knight of the medieval Order of the Temple

explanation.surface: A king and a knight of a military order beheaded, held up as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing heads' strips the R from REX and the T from TEMPLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An exemplar is a perfect example, someone or something serving as a pattern to copy.

clue.text: Car attendant

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a long-running British Ford hatchback model
second meaning: a companion who accompanies someone, a chaperone or guard

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a car park or petrol pump attendant, but it is two separate meanings; the Ford Escort is a long-running British Ford.
explanation.definitionFit: Escort names a Ford model and also a person who accompanies another for protection or company.

clue.text: He lays slates, 50 in a row

indicators.note: in places the Roman fifty inside the word for a row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A roofer putting down fifty slates in a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiler is a tradesman who covers roofs with slates or tiles.

clue.text: Ashes of the French saint

parts.note: du is French for of the

explanation.surface: The remains of a French saint, as relics.
explanation.definitionFit: Dust is the powdered remains of a body, as in 'ashes to ashes, dust to dust'.

clue.text: Trivial insolence; quaint variety

indicators.note: a variety is a different version, so the letters are mixed into another form

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict that rudeness and a quaint style are both trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inconsequential has no importance, unimportant and not worth notice.

clue.text: Course records gaining award

indicators.note: gaining means the records take on the award at the end

parts.note: EPs are extended-play records
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A racecourse's music releases winning an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom is an English racecourse, home of the Derby; the OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs is a racecourse in Surrey that hosts the Derby horse race.

clue.text: Station wagon, say, in race, overturned

indicators.note: in puts the word for say inside the flipped word
overturned means the word race is flipped and read the other way

parts.note: to state is to say

explanation.surface: A station wagon, for instance, flipping over during a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example', but it is a verb giving a synonym that sits inside the flipped race.
explanation.definitionFit: Station wagon is the American term for the British estate car, a car with a long rear load space.
